L249@P2: 6. EXPERIMENTAL METHODOLOGY
L250@P2: We compare the proposed LSU approach to the conventional one
L251@P2: using the whole image, and hereafter, named as global spectral
L252@P2: unmixing (GSU), to induce the endmembers and estimate the corresponding abundances. We test the two approaches using the Cuprite
L253@P2: dataset [12] (see Fig. 2). The scene was taken by the NASA’s
L254@P2: AVIRIS sensor and covers the Cuprite mining district in western
L255@P2: Nevada, USA.
L256@P2: We define the experimental unmixing process as the application
L257@P2: of the Vertex Component Analysis (VCA) [13] to induce the endmembers from a given set of pixels. The VCA is run 10 times per
L258@P2: region in order to avoid issues due to its stochastic nature, retaining the set of endmembers with maximum simplex volume. Then,
L259@P2: the unmixing process estimates the abundances corresponding to the
L260@P2: induced endmembers and the given set of pixels by solving the optimization problem in (2) with sparsity, τ = 10−3
L261@P2: , and without sparsity, τ = 0.
L262@P2: For the case of the GSU, the unmixing process is run over the
L263@P2: whole data set. For the LSU, we have implemented the proposed
L264@P2: BPT-based LSU (Sec. 5), where the BPT representation is built using the first order parametric model (3) and the merging criterion defined in (4). Then, the unmixing process is independently run over
L265@P2: each node of the BPT representation in order to find the optimal partition given by the two pruning strategies (7) and (8) using as the

L383@P3: 8. CONCLUSIONS
L384@P3: We have introduced a novel general approach based on the local
L385@P3: spectral unmixing of hyperspectral images in order to overcome the
L386@P3: limitations of the classical global spectral unmixing when there are
L387@P3: several mixtures of materials or spectral variability due to illumination and atmospheric effects. We have also proposed a BPT-based
L388@P3: implementation of local spectral unmixing. Results show that the
L389@P3: proposed approach yield better reconstruction errors, suggesting that
L390@P3: it is able to cope with these issues. We concluded that this a promising methodology that requires of further work to completely understand the nuances of the proposed BPT-based local spectral unmixing. We will focus on the use of BPT representations built over an
L391@P3: unmixing-based model and merging criterion, on the evaluation of
L392@P3: the proposed local spectral unmixing in more depth, with real and
L393@P3: synthetic data, in terms of reconstruction quality but also in terms
L394@P3: of abundances estimation. Also, we need to explore the unmixing
L395@P3: information contained through the spatial scales, and make an effort
L396@P3: to reduce the computational burden.
